memories.author: D03
memories.text:
PRESENTING COMPLAINT: Routine review of epilepsy, anxiety and chronic urticaria.
EXAMINATION: BP 118/72 mmHg, weight 68 kg, height 1.70 m, BMI 23.5 (overweight). Cardiovascular and respiratory systems normal. Skin shows mild dermographism, no active wheals.
IMPRESSION: Stable epilepsy on levetiracetam and lamotrigine. Generalised anxiety disorder controlled on escitalopram 5 mg OD and buspirone 5 mg BD. Chronic urticaria mild, on levocetirizine 5 mg OD and cetirizine 10 mg HS.
ARRANGEMENTS: Continue current medications. Order fasting lipid profile, fasting blood sugar, serum sodium, serum creatinine, TSH, haemoglobin, CBC with eosinophils and thyroid function test. Schedule EEG. Advise weight reduction through balanced diet and regular activity. Return if seizures worsen, panic attacks, chest pain, breathlessness, fever >39°C or blood in stools.

memories.author: D03
memories.text: Electroencephalogram (EEG) performed with 16-channel montage during awake and hyperventilation phases. Background rhythm shows symmetric 8-10 Hz alpha activity, no focal slowing. No epileptiform discharges, spikes or sharp waves detected. No photic driving abnormalities. Interpretation: No evidence of epileptiform activity; study consistent with well-controlled epilepsy on current regimen.

memories.author: patient
memories.text: Over the past few weeks I have felt more nervous and restless, with trouble concentrating at work. I also noticed a mild increase in itchy wheals on my arms, especially in the evenings, which respond partially to cetirizine. My sleep is okay but I wake up feeling tense. I am worried my anxiety meds might need adjustment.

memories.author: D03
memories.text:
PRESENTING COMPLAINT: Increased anxiety symptoms and mild urticaria flare.
EXAMINATION: BP 120/74 mmHg, weight 68.5 kg, BMI 23.7 (overweight). No tachycardia. Skin shows scattered small wheals on forearms, no angioedema. Neurologic exam normal.
IMPRESSION: Generalised anxiety disorder with modest symptom escalation; likely needing antidepressant dose titration. Chronic urticaria mild, responsive to antihistamines but requiring increased daytime control. Epilepsy remains seizure-free.
ARRANGEMENTS: Increase escitalopram to 10 mg OD; continue buspirone 5 mg BD. Increase levocetirizine to 10 mg OD; keep cetirizine 10 mg HS for breakthrough. Reinforce seizure precautions. Return if seizures develop, severe panic, difficulty breathing, swelling of lips/tongue, or widespread rash.

memories.author: D03
memories.text: Repeat EEG performed to ensure ongoing stability. Awake recording shows posterior dominant rhythm 9 Hz, symmetric. No epileptiform discharges, spikes or slow waves. Hyperventilation and photic stimulation did not provoke abnormalities. Interpretation: No epileptiform activity; epilepsy remains well controlled on current levetiracetam and lamotrigine regimen.

memories.author: D03
memories.text:
PRESENTING COMPLAINT: Routine review; patient reports stable mood and infrequent urticaria.
EXAMINATION: BP 119/71 mmHg, weight 68 kg, BMI 23.5 (overweight). Skin clear, no wheals. No neurologic deficits.
IMPRESSION: Anxiety well controlled on escitalopram 10 mg OD and buspirone 5 mg BD. Chronic urticaria minimal, current antihistamine regimen adequate. Epilepsy seizure-free for >6 months.
ARRANGEMENTS: Continue current medications. Annual fasting lipid profile, fasting blood sugar, serum sodium, creatinine, TSH, haemoglobin, CBC eosinophils, thyroid function tests ordered. Influenza vaccine offered and administered today (0.5 mL IM). Return if seizures, worsening anxiety, chest pain, breathlessness, fever >39°C or bleeding.
